sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized anti-FLAG M2 FACS sorting (L2); GPI-anchored surface expression confirmed by PI-PLC cleavage assay monitored by flow cytometry (L3, L4). No ligand-binding or functional assay reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: The topology landmarks place the signal peptide at residues 1–19 and the mature N-terminus at residue 20. Python lookup of the numbered sequence confirms residue 19 = S and residue 20 = L, so insert_after_residue=19 places the FLAG tag at the extracellular mature N-terminus, exactly where the paper describes. LYPD8 is GPI-anchored with no TM domain; the entire region 20–237 is extracellular, so there is no TM boundary constraint to evaluate. L2–L4 independently confirm that the FLAG-tagged full-length construct reaches the cell surface in the correct GPI-anchored orientation. Full-length hLYPD8 coding sequence with a FLAG tag inserted immediately downstream of the predicted N-terminal signal sequence (residues 1–19), stably expressed in HEK293T cells. Non-permeabilized anti-FLAG M2 FACS confirmed cell-surface display; PI-PLC treatment (which cleaves GPI-anchored proteins) abolished the surface signal, confirming GPI-anchored surface expression of the FLAG-tagged construct.

sources.claim: A FLAG-tagged sequence was inserted into the total mLypd8 and hLYPD8 coding sequence immediately downstream of the predicted N-terminal signal sequence.

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) derive from the same publication (PMC5725809) and describe a single FLAG-tag insertion site at the mature N-terminus of hLYPD8 (after signal peptide cleavage at residue 19). L1 pins the position; L2 validates surface display by non-permeabilized FACS; L3 and L4 confirm GPI-anchored surface expression via PI-PLC cleavage. No internal loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or functional assays are reported in the ledger. Because LYPD8 is GPI-anchored with no transmembrane domain, the entire ectodomain (residues 20–237) is extracellular; the N-terminal mature junction is the only terminus accessible for a surface tag. No other sites are supported by the ledger.
